title: VPC Shield: Terraform module for SG/NACL/private-DNS egress controls + healthchecks
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Purpose: Provide a single, opinionated Terraform module — "vpc_shield" — that implements production-grade network security controls for Redwood Private (VPC) deployments. The module must manage Security Groups (SGs), Network ACLs (NACLs), Route53 private hosted zones (private DNS), and enforce egress policies (allow-lists, explicit deny rules, optional egress-proxy integration). It will include automated health checks and a lightweight upgrade path to ensure safe rollout across existing customer VPC stacks.

Scope: AWS-first (Route53, SG, NACL). Support for cross-account private zone associations and association with VPCs created by other stacks. Module should be reusable across host accounts and customer-managed VPCs. Ship inputs for common patterns (default-deny flags, managed-ports, egress-allowlist CIDRs/domains, integration toggles for in-cluster egress-proxy). Provide outputs with taggable ARNs and summary policy metadata for console and auditing.

Non-goals: Implementing full network firewall appliance (e.g., AWS Network Firewall rulesets) or detailed per-application microsegmentation. GCP/Azure parity is out-of-scope for initial release.

Design notes and constraints:
- Security posture: default-deny egress and ingress by default; explicit allowlists for required services (NTP, KMS, S3 endpoints when applicable, monitoring, etc.).
- Layering: SGs enforce instance-level stateful policies; NACLs provide stateless subnet-level hardening to catch misconfigured routes. Module must provide both and document recommended ordering and common pitfalls.
- Private DNS: Manage Route53 private hosted zones + cross-account associations. Provide an option to create conditional forwarders for on-prem environments (via Route53 resolver rules) and a mode to only create zone associations (no zone ownership) for customers that bring their own zone.
- Egress policy modes: 
  * permissive (default for existing customers upgrading)
  * strict-allow (recommended for regulated customers)
  * proxy-enforced (integrates with an optional HTTP/TCP egress proxy; adds SG/NACL rules allowing only proxy endpoints).
- Health checks: Terraform-level validation + runtime health checks. Implement Terratest suite that does plan/apply in a test account, verifies security group rules, NACL entries, and DNS resolution against the private zone. Add an optional Lambda-based scheduled health check that verifies egress rules and reports violations to a CloudWatch metric/Slack webhook.
- Upgrade considerations: Provide a 2-phase apply path for non-disruptive upgrades: (1) feature flags and additive resources, (2) safe swing to stricter defaults with migration guidance. Include a migration.md in the module.

Compatibility: Must be compatible with Terraform 1.5+ and AWS provider >= 5.x. Use provider aliases for cross-account associations. Use minimal external modules; prefer native resources to ease audits.

Outputs expected (examples): vpc_shield_sg_ids, vpc_shield_nacl_ids, private_zone_id, egress_policy_summary (JSON-string).

Why this matters: Customers running Redwood Private demand predictable, auditable network controls that are easy to adopt and upgrade without causing outages. This module standardizes best practices and reduces one-off patches during customer onboarding and upgrades.
acceptance_criteria: Module implements SGs and NACLs with sensible defaults (default-deny inbound, configurable egress allowlists)
Route53 private hosted zone creation + cross-account association or association-only mode is covered and tested
Egress policy modes (permissive, strict-allow, proxy-enforced) are configurable and documented
Terratest (or equivalent) integration exists and runs in CI verifying rules and DNS resolution
Non-disruptive upgrade path documented and validated in staging (migration.md and sample upgrade plan)
Healthcheck Lambda (optional) deployed via module or companion module and emits CloudWatch metrics on violations
Module passes security review and automated policy checks (tfsec & sentinel minimal gates)
